title: Expose a finite nonlinear identification construction with its acquisition costs
statement: The supplied finite floating experiment reconstructs two six-site real symmetric cyclic Hamiltonian sources related by an orthogonal port-fixing gauge, using one-port complex fields, linear frequency/control acquisition and a distributed Kerr pulse. Distributed nonlinear slices differ where the displayed off/port-only/isotropic controls agree; shorter pulses reduce the displayed aligned reconstruction error. One finite simulated model, not a general algorithmic capability or novelty result. Actual frequency gaps, port weights, Hankel/readout/control conditioning, supplied distributed nonlinear primitive, pulse extrapolation and ignored imaginary/antisymmetric components are paid.113calls/684portreads per instance plus preparation/readout/pulse work are reported; elapsed Python time is not physical runtime. No finite-error certificate or hardware. The laterN596/N597source pointer was delivered AFTER this early experiment; those prior constructions retain their own stability/conditioning disagreement and access models.
